newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa budget to direct local shares next week.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa budget to direct local shares next week.

text.p: The South African budget will give direction to shares next week while the futures contract close-out will add to market volatility, dealers and portfolio managers said.

Finance Minister Trevor Manuel will present the budget on Wednesday and dealers and portfolio managers said the market would be quiet ahead of the presentation and then move in line with plans released during the budget speech.

"In the early part of the week it will be quiet in the run-up to the budget. There will not be much in terms of tax. The key interest will be whether anything will be included on foreign exchange controls," Malcolm Chapman, managing director at Absa Asset Management, told Reuters.
Dealers said there were also rumours about the relaxing of foreign exchange controls to the extent that institutions could be allowed more than the 10 percent permitted at present.

Chapman said if there is nothing on exchange controls then long-term interest rates will move down and equities would rise. If there is something, then short-term interest rates will go up while equities would decline.
Rien van Veen, an equities dealer at Investec Asset Management, said there were rumours that the Marketable Securities Tax could fall away which would boost the market.
"If MST falls away we might see a spike in the market," he said.
Mike Brown, economist at Societe Generale Frankel Pollack, said there had been few leaks of the budget's content.
"Normally you have an idea of what will happen, but we will now have to wait and see. It is much less clear but there are lots of rumours," he said.
The futures close-out on March 17 is seen adding to volatility on the market.
"This is the last week before the futures close-out and there are 50,000 open contracts. We will see some volatility next week," a dealers said.
Portfolio managers were mixed on gold shares and said the budget would have minimal effect on them as they react to the gold price which in turn is directed by news of gold sales by central banks.
Some said they would be a non-event while others said they might try to regain some losses after hefty falls seen during this week.
The market will also look to the January Producer Price Inflation figure due for release on Thursday.
A Reuter consensus forecast of 10 economists forecast the PPI would rise 0.9 percent month-on-month or 9.4 percent year-on-year. The average was drawn from a range of 0.8 to 1.1 percent.
